_comment: T470 — the Epic stage model as CONFIGURATION (FR-ESK-015). Same pattern as governance.config.json: a stage sequence hard-coded in a check is a process nobody agreed to. The counts here are fixed by the specification — seven stages (FR-ESK-001), three posture kinds (FR-ESK-020), two Epic kinds (FR-ESK-024), twelve DOR conditions (FR-ESK-012) — and G-26-01 asserts them. The contents are configuration and are asserted for structure only, so this file can change without editing a test.
_derivedVsDeclared: Stage and DOR results are DERIVED from the file tree. Epic kind, posture and waivers are DECLARED by a person in governance/epic-declarations.json. Nothing crosses that line: a person never writes a stage, a machine never infers intent.

stages.name: Clarified
stages.evidence: spec.md contains a '## Clarifications' heading and at least one '### Session <date>'
stages._why: FR-ESK-018. Derived from a recorded session, NOT from the absence of [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers — absence would mark every freshly written spec as clarified before the step ever ran. A session that asked nothing still counts: the artifact records that the step RAN, not that it found something (FR-ESK-017).

stages.name: Checklisted
stages.evidence: at least one file in checklists/ and zero unchecked items across them

stages.name: Planned
stages._nextWhy: DEF-026-007 — a parent design carries no tasks (FR-ESK-024); telling it to generate them re-creates the duplication D-18/D-19 exist to prevent. Same appliesTo semantics as the DOR conditions: absence means every kind.

stages.name: Analyzed
stages._why: FR-ESK-019. The analysis step used to print its findings and leave nothing behind, which would have made this the one stage in the journey with no artifact — a hole in FR-ESK-003 on the day it was written.

stages.name: Ready
stages.evidence: every DOR condition passes, or is covered by a valid waiver

_postureNote: FR-ESK-004 — posture is an OVERLAY on the derived stage, never a replacement for it: an Epic that is Held is still at whatever stage its artifacts prove, and clearing the posture resumes it there with no stage information lost. All three block readiness. Keeping every kind blocking means a recorded stop always means not Ready, so no reader has to remember which kinds are which. A non-blocking 'Deferred' was rejected: an Epic simultaneously postponed and Ready is a contradiction the register would have to explain every time it was read. Absence is not a posture — an Epic stopped with nothing declared reads 'stalled' (FR-ESK-006).

delivery.meaning: Produces tasks and is implemented. The default when nothing is declared

parent-design.meaning: Holds requirements and design for child Epics; deliberately carries no tasks

dorConditions.reads: spec.md — no '[NEEDS CLARIFICATION' outside inline code

dorConditions.condition: SRS traceability populated; uncovered requirements name a back-fill owner
Requirements checklist present and fully resolved
Plan exists and its Constitution Check records no FAIL

dorConditions._why: FR-ESK-024 — a parent design deliberately carries no tasks and is never evaluated for readiness. Judging it on a task list it is defined not to have produced a permanent non-finding on every run. Reported NOT APPLICABLE rather than passed: Constitution IX forbids reporting an unrun check as passing, and a parent design has not satisfied this condition — the condition does not reach it.

dorConditions.condition: Every implementation task pairs with a test or conformance check
dorConditions._why: Same as DOR-07 — it reads tasks.md, which a parent design does not have.

dorConditions.condition: Analysis recorded with zero blocking findings
defects/ exists with no open records

_dorNote: FR-ESK-010 — this list IS the written Definition of Ready: the complete set of conditions an Epic must satisfy before /speckit-implement may run against it. Evaluation is TOTAL, not short-circuiting (FR-ESK-013): every condition is evaluated and every failure listed, so one pass tells a reader everything outstanding. It is also FRESH, never stamped — amending a spec after the DOR passed withdraws readiness on the next run, with no explicit invalidation step.
_waiverNote: Reused from governance.config.json 'owners', not re-declared — a second list would drift and authorise owners governance did not. A waiver covers exactly one DOR condition for one Epic, carries a reason and an expiry, and makes the Epic read 'Ready (waived)' and never plain Ready (FR-ESK-023). An expired waiver FAILS THE BUILD. Waivers exist because a gate with no legitimate exception path is the kind that gets edited rather than obeyed.
